fields.title: What the User Sees During Retries
fields.keyTakeaway: The duration of retries for a synchronous operation is determined by user patience, not system capabilities, and after exhaustion you need a product outcome, not an error message.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: The system retries the request three times for a total of 23 seconds. What happens on the screen during this time?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Resilience mechanisms are designed by engineers, but their manifestations are seen by the user. Twenty-three seconds of honest waiting is worse than a failure at five if the person does not understand what they are waiting for.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: Rule: **total retry time must fit into user patience, not system capabilities.**
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: For a synchronous operation where a person is waiting, a reasonable limit is 5–10 seconds. This is one or two attempts, not three with exponential backoff.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: For a background operation, retries can last minutes and hours — the constraint there is different: **relevance.** An order notification delivered six hours later is harmful. Hence the rule from `IN2-N4-L1` about messages older than two hours.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *How long to wait synchronously before moving to deferred.* "Didn't work out in 8 seconds — we accept and confirm with a notification". *What to show between attempts.* Text escalation from `IN1-N3-L2`. *What to do after exhaustion.* Failure, deferred processing, or switching to Plan B.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: An important case — **different behavior for different operations.** Payment: we retry longer because the alternative is worse. Avatar upload: one attempt, failure immediately — the person will press it themselves.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Checkout: three attempts, 2/6/15 seconds, up to 23 seconds total. The screen escalates text, after 10 seconds a "Minimize" button appears with the promise of a notification. 8% use it.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: Promo code check: one attempt, 2-second timeout, on failure — "Failed to check code, please try again". It makes no sense to retry here: the person is right there and will press it themselves, and waiting is annoying.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Sending a notification to the store: up to 10 attempts over an hour, then a failure queue and a call from an operator. There is no human in the loop, delivery is what matters.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Supplier catalog update: 3 attempts with intervals up to 5 minutes, then we work on cache and notify. The user does not know about this at all.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Long retries hold resources. A hundred waiting operations of 20 seconds each mean a hundred occupied connections, and at peak load this in itself becomes a problem.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: The duration of retries for a synchronous operation is determined by user patience, not system capabilities, and after exhaustion you need a product outcome, not an error message.
